input.question: Why is it not naturally possible to get rid of moles?
input.ground_truth: If it worked, you'd see it being used by licensed physicians, and a vastly marked up "prescription strength" honey. To quote commedian Dara O'Briain: > "I'm sorry, 'herbal medicine', 'Oh, herbal medicine's been around for thousands of years!' Indeed it has, and then we tested it all, and the stuff that worked became 'medicine', and the rest of it is just a nice bowl of soup and some potpourri, so knock yourselves out.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why is it not naturally possible to get rid of moles?

Answer:

response.prediction: Okay! Imagine your skin is like a big garden. In this garden, there are little spots called moles. These moles are like tiny flowers or freckles that grow on your skin because of how your body is made. Just like you can’t pick out every single blade of grass from the garden easily, it’s really hard (and not normal) to get rid of every mole on your skin. Our bodies grow them naturally, and trying to get rid of them on your own isn’t safe or easy. Doctors can sometimes help if you really want them gone, but usually, moles are just part of what makes your skin special!
